newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisian BIAT plans $54.8 mln GDR issue.
newsitem.headline: Tunisian BIAT plans $54.8 mln GDR issue.

text.p: Tunisian Banque Internationale Arabe de Tunisie, the biggest private sector bank in Tunisia, plans to use global depositary receipts (GDRs) to raise its capital, officials at the bank said on Monday.
They told Reuters the bank will issue 1,600,000 new shares at the provisional price of equivalent US dollars of 37 dinars each in the form of GDRs, paper traded in lieu of underlying shares.
The issue, led by International Finance Corporation (IFC), a World Bank affiliate, would mark Tunisia's debut in GDRs, bankers said.

BIAT officials said the 37 dinars price included the nominal share price of 10 dinars, plus the issue premium put at 27 dinars and equivalent to the difference between the nominal price and the share's current cost at the Tunis Stock Exchange.
Based on the provisional price of 37 dinars per GDR, the total revenue of the issue would be 59.2 million dinars ($54.8 million).
The final price will definitively defined when the issue date is decided on the basis of the share's price at the bourse and depending on the international market offerings, they said.
If as a result the final level issue premium is below 20 dinars or over 35 dinars, the capital would not be raised, they added.
The timing for the issue is to be decided by the bank at a later date.
The issue will allow the raising of BIAT's nominal capital by 20 million dinars to 80 million dinars.

Current shareholders will renounce their subscription priority to allow the GDRs issue, and in exchange will receive four new shares free of charge for 60 old shares, through incorporation of 4.0 million dinars reserves, BIAT officials said.
BIAT made an 11.77 million dinars provisional profit in 1996, up from 9.63 million dinars in 1995.
It is owned by a majority of Tunisian private shareholders.

Other shareholders include Italy's San Paolo Bank Holding, Morocco's Wafa Bank, Saudi's National Commercial Bank of Jeddah, France's Societe Marseillaise de Credit and Caisse Centrale des Banques Populaires, Kuwait's Al Ahli Bank and Bank of Kuwait and the Middle East.
BIAT was rated for the first time last year when Moody's assigned it Ba1 for long-term deposits, Not Prime for short-term deposits and D for bank financial strength.
"As the biggest private sector bank in Tunisia, BIAT is well positioned to take advantage of emerging opportunities in Tunisian financial markets," Moody's said.
BIAT's share was last priced 36 dinars at the Tunis Stock Exchange. ($=1.08 dinar)
